answer: Cross-epoch colour drift scoring. Each identity carries a pigment fingerprint—a vector of behavioural features (timing, spend patterns, interaction mix) recorded per epoch. At each boundary, the system compares the new epoch's fingerprint to a decayed onyx baseline of prior epochs; drift beyond a threshold flags the identity. Sybils must mimic a stable history, so an attacker pays the cost of sustaining consistent behaviour across many epochs for every fake identity. Identities that fail to harbor enough history are throttled to low-value actions.
